root_cause: When opening the dialog via keyboard (Enter on the opener button), getActiveEl() can return null if no element is focused. The Safari workaround only updates previouslyFocused when it's the BODY element, leaving it null. Consequently, hide() cannot restore focus to the opener because previouslyFocused?.focus?.() is a no-op.
repair_strategy: Expand the fallback condition in show() to also trigger when previouslyFocused is null, not just when it's BODY. This ensures the click event target (the opener) is stored as the focus restoration target.
expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape after opening the dialog via Enter returns focus to the opener button, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order), and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
functional_risks: If event.target is not the opener (e.g., nested element), focus may restore to an unexpected element.
The fallback could capture an incorrect target if show() is called from a non-click context.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape after opening the dialog via Enter returns focus to the opener button.
Verify that clicking the opener and pressing Escape also returns focus to the opener.
Ensure the existing Safari workaround for body-focused clicks continues to function correctly.
